articles.title: ‘I get emotional thinking I’ll be off the streets by Christmas’
articles.summary: Homeless people and charities react as work to help find everyone accommodation by Christmas begins.
articles.body:
Work has begun to try to meet the prime minister’s pledge to offer all rough sleepers a route off the streets before Christmas.

Andy Burnham made the promise on his first day in the job and the government has since allocated more than £12m to the West of England Combined Authority to tackle homelessness over the next three years.

In Bristol, the number of people sleeping rough has increased steadily since Covid, with the council's monthly street count now approaching the highest-ever recorded.

One charity said it was "confident" accommodation could be found for everyone currently in need but that long-term success would depend on making sure the right support and housing was available.

"They actually came to me today and said they're going to house me from three o'clock this afternoon,” Dexter, who has been sleeping rough for 18 months, said.

He said he was delighted to have somewhere to go.

"More than anything it's really, really boring,” he said. “The worst bit of it is people just walk by. You're kind of invisible a lot of the time.

"Them coming and offering me housing today was quite a surprise. It came out of nowhere."

Dexter said he had not previously asked for help because he had not wanted to be separated from his dog, Reginald.

He has been told, though, that there was now space for them both.

"I'm pretty chuffed with that because I can't cope without this one [Reginald]," he explained. "He keeps me sane on a day-to-day basis, gets me up in the morning."

Dexter said he became homeless as a result of experiencing depression and alcoholism after losing a close friend.

"There's been a lot of times where I've felt incredibly vulnerable," he said.

"I don't think I'll find myself out here again. I want to get back towards doing some work."

Patrick said he had been homeless on-and-off for eight years, since a family breakdown.

"I lost my family and my job in one fell swoop," he said. "It sent me a bit depressed, I couldn't cope on my own.

"My self-esteem went down and I just haven't been able to get back on my feet."

He said his most recent shelter placement lasted about two months, ending after he had friends over when overnight guests were not allowed.

"They gave me all these rules but they didn't help me to cope with being lonely indoors,” he said.

Patrick admits that the prospect of being responsible for bills was also daunting but he said with the right support he thinks he could succeed.

He said being off the streets by Christmas would mean "happiness, security" to him.

"I get emotional thinking about it," he said. "A future - it would mean a lot.

"I hope they're not lying. I would really like to be housed."

St Mungos delivers homeless outreach services on behalf of the city council.

David Ingerslev, from the charity, said: "I am confident we'll have an offer for everyone.”

He said the charity was trying to set up a range of options to meet different people's needs in different locations across the city.

"There are women-only spaces, spaces where pets can be accepted, places with different amounts of support of available," he said.

But Ingerslev said it was "a really big logistical challenge" to have the right places available for the right people at the right time.

He estimated there would need to be about 200 extra bed spaces in the city to meet demand.

"We're preparing for all eventualities," he said.

"Some people won't accept the offers and where they don't we're going to put additional support in place for people affected by things like mental health issues, learning difficulties, or substance misuse.”

Ingerslev said one of the biggest challenges was finding something more permanent for people placed in an emergency shelter.

Supported accommodation is often the best option but all 900 of the city’s beds are currently taken.

"The move-on from [supported housing] is much slower than it used to be,” Ingerslev said.

"We need to unlock the supported accommodation that we have."

However, that requires affordable housing for people to move into and Ingerslev said high housing costs in the city were at the root of the problem because they increase demand for social housing and make it harder to buy potential supported accommodation properties.

"It's an attractive city to come and live in,” he said "but that's contributing to the pressure on the housing market."

If you see someone sleeping rough, you can contact StreetLink to connect them to support.

articles.title: '560% above known income': Lokayukta unearths Rs 7.6 crore assets of MP forest officer
articles.summary: BHOPAL: The Lokayukta's Special Police Establishment (SPE) on Saturday raided the government residence and office of Sanjeev Kumar Sharma, assistant
articles.body: BHOPAL: The Lokayukta's Special Police Establishment (SPE) on Saturday raided the government residence and office of Sanjeev Kumar Sharma, assistant director of Satpura Tiger Reserve in Pachmarhi, and his private residence in Chhindwara in a disproportionate assets case, claiming to have unearthed assets worth around Rs 7.6 crore.The searches, conducted by multiple teams of the Lokayukta SPE's Bhopal division, revealed Rs 26.36 lakh in cash, gold jewellery weighing 2.528kg, silver weighing 1.656kg, several vehicles and two hospitality properties, including a resort and a villa, according to the agency's preliminary assessment.The Lokayukta SPE said an initial verification had indicated that Sharma allegedly possessed assets 228% higher than his known sources of income.However, the searches reportedly revealed properties estimated at around Rs 7.6 crore, which the agency said were approximately 560% disproportionate to his known income.The raids followed confidential information that Sharma had allegedly accumulated assets disproportionate to his income in the names of his wife and other private individuals.A case was registered against him under Section 13(1)(b), read with Section 13(2), of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, as amended in 2018. Search warrants were subsequently obtained from a court before teams moved in at the three locations.Among the assets recovered, gold jewellery weighing 2.528kg was valued at approximately Rs 3.5 crore, while 1.656kg of silver was estimated to be worth Rs 2.94 lakh. Cash amounting to Rs 26.36 lakh was also found.The Lokayukta SPE identified two hospitality properties — Ecotel Resort, estimated to be worth around Rs 2 crore, and Serenity The Villa, valued at approximately Rs 1 crore. Their final valuation is yet to be completed.Investigators also found documents relating to the purchase and sale of land at the searched premises. As many as 28 documents were seized for examination.The agency said the valuation of the resorts and other properties, along with scrutiny of the land transactions, could further increase the estimated value of the assets.Vehicles found during the searches included a Mahindra Scorpio, a Mahindra KUV, a Bullet motorcycle and a scooter, collectively valued at around Rs 31.2 lakh. Household articles and other possessions were estimated to be worth approximately Rs 50 lakh.Lokayukta director general Yogesh Deshmukh had directed intensified action against corruption. The operation was carried out under the guidance of deputy inspector general Manoj Kumar Singh.Teams were led by deputy superintendent of police Virendra Singh, who conducted the preliminary verification, and DSP Ajay Mishra, with support from DSP Bhaiyalal Prajapati and inspectors Rajni Tiwari, Ghanshyam Maskole and Neetu Kusaria, besides other personnel from the Bhopal division.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: Breakup revenge: Youth kills ex-partner’s dogs, video-calls her to show ‘proof’
articles.summary: Kolkata: Youth in Bikramgarh allegedly killed ex live-in partner’s two pet dogs to avenge breakup, video-called her as proof; Jadavpur police detained him.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A chilling case of animal cruelty has triggered widespread outrage in Bikramgarh neighbourhood as a youth reportedly killed both the pet dogs of his former live-in partner inside their flat on Saturday afternoon, ostensibly to exact revenge over their breakup.He even went on to make a video call to the girl and showed her how he had hanged one of the two dogs by a noose.Cops from the Jadavpur Police Station detained the accused, Sanjib Bhattacharya, from the Bikramgarh apartment following protests by residents of the area and animal rights activists.According to police, Bhattacharya had been living in a rented flat in Bikramgarh with his partner, a DJ. After their relationship went southward recently, the DJ decided to move out of the apartment but left her two pet dogs behind in Bhattacharya’s care, a neighbour said.Enraged by her decision to leave him, Bhattacharya apparently took out his anger on the helpless animals on Saturday. Animal rights activists claimed he made a video call to the DJ during which he reportedly shocked her by showing one of her pet dogs hanging by a noose around its neck.Terrified by the scene on the video call, the DJ immediately forwarded the footage and telephoned a youth in the Bikramgarh neighbourhood, pleading with him to go to the flat immediately and check on the dog.When the youth and some other residents of the area entered the apartment, they discovered that not one but both of the woman’s pet dogs had been killed. While one of the dogs was reportedly hanged with a noose, the other one—a puppy—was killed by bashing its head in with a brick, an animal activist said.Blood was spattered across the floor of the apartment. Residents claimed that they found Bhattacharya boiling water in the kitchen, raising suspicions that he intended to pour scalding water over the animals. Another group said he could have been boiling water to wash away evidence.As the horrifying news spread in the locality, actor and animal lover Debleena Dutt, accompanied by members of animal welfare organisations, visited the spot in the evening. Cops from the Jadavpur Police Station also reached the flat and detained Bhattacharya, who was reportedly found “mentally unstable”. Those gathered in the neighbourhood said despite the extreme brutality of his act, Bhattacharya did not seem to show any remorse.Demanding stringent legal action and post-mortem for the two dogs, Dutt recounted her interaction with the accused at the flat.“On learning about the incident, I went there. The accused gave his own name and proudly said he had been living with his girlfriend. He said that after she left him, he killed one of her dogs by hanging it with a noose and that he killed a puppy by smashing its head with a brick. He said he did it to take revenge on his girlfriend. I then went to the police station and helped register a complaint. I have requested for a postmortem report for both dogs as we believe the second dog was hit repeatedly on his head to death,” she said.Police confirmed that the accused was detained for questioning and that legal formalities were underway.(with inputs from Sarthak Ganguly)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Projeto leva assistência especializada a criadores de ovinos em RR | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudantes e professores de zootecnia, veterinária e agronomia oferecem orientação sobre nutrição e prevenção de doenças no rebanho. Ação tem prática em propriedades.
articles.summary: Estudantes e professores de zootecnia, veterinária e agronomia oferecem orientação sobre nutrição e prevenção de doenças no rebanho. Ação tem prática em propriedades.
articles.body:
Criadores de ovelhas e carneiros de Boa Vista podem contar com acompanhamento especializado do projeto Ovino Plus . A iniciativa, desenvolvida pelo Centro de Ciências Agrárias da Universidade Federal de Roraima (UFRR), orienta os produtores rurais sobre alimentação , manejo e prevenção de doenças nos rebanhos.

A equipe reúne professores e 20 estudantes de zootecnia, medicina veterinária e agronomia. O grupo vai até as propriedades participantes para acompanhar os animais de perto.

A coordenadora do projeto e professora de Zootecnia, Gisele Fagundes, explica que o serviço surgiu para atender a uma demanda local. “A gente leva esse conhecimento técnico e científico para o produtor, justamente para fortalecer a ovinocultura [criação de ovelhas] aqui, porque ainda é algo escasso”, afirma.

Durante as visitas, os alunos montam dietas , avaliam a nutrição e monitoram a saúde dos rebanhos . Eles também pesam os animais todos os meses e coletam fezes para exames que identificam parasitas.

Projeto da UFRR, Ovino Plus, oferece assistência técnica gratuita a produtores com criações de ovinos. — Foto: Raquel Maia/Amazônia Agro

A ação no campo também funciona como aula prática para os universitários. A estudante de Medicina Veterinária Thaís Tobias conta que o contato com os criadores permite adaptar as melhorias para cada realidade.

"Acompanhamos os resultados ao longo dos meses e percebemos que o nosso trabalho está sendo bem aplicado e que o produtor também está satisfeito”, relata.

Na área de saúde, os criadores aprendem a prevenir doenças, aplicar vermífugos, realizar a tosa e o casqueamento (corte das unhas dos animais). Esses cuidados mantêm a qualidade do rebanho e evitam prejuízos financeiros ao produtor.

Os produtores interessados em receber o acompanhamento devem procurar a secretaria do Centro de Ciências Agrárias, que fica no Campus Cauamé da UFRR, na BR-174, região do Monte Cristo.

Projeto Ovino Plus é oportunidade para estudantes da UFRR iniciarem atuação na área junto com produtores. — Foto: Raquel Maia/Amazônia Agro

articles.summary: O Inmet alerta para tempestade em Minas Gerais com ventos de até 60 km/h e riscos de alagamentos em Belo Horizonte e outras 843 cidades neste domingo.
articles.body:
Municípios que estão sob aviso amarelo de tempestade — Foto: Inmet

Mais de 800 cidades de Minas Gerais , incluindo Belo Horizonte e Região Metropolitana, estão incluídas no aviso amarelo para tempestade do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet). O aviso é válido ao longo de todo o domingo (15). Apenas parte do Noroeste do estado não está incluído no aviso.

O órgão alerta para volume de água entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou 50 por dia, além de ventos entre 40 e 60 km/h. Existe ainda risco para corte de energia elétrica, queda de galhos de árvores, alagamentos e de descargas elétricas.

A orientação do Inmet para o estado é que, em caso de chuva, a população não se abrigue debaixo de árvores nem estacione veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda. Caso seja possível, outra recomendação é desligar os aparelhos elétricos e quadro geral de energia.

Em caso de emergência, a Defesa Civil (199) e o Corpo de Bombeiros (193) devem ser acionados. O aviso meteorológico cobre a maior parte do estado, além de outras regiões próximas, como o Espírito Santo, o Rio de Janeiro e São Paulo.

O alerta inclui cidades na Região Central Mineira, Zona da Mata, Vale do Rio Doce, Oeste de Minas, Sul, Sudoeste de Minas, Campo das Vertentes, Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, Jequitinhonha, Vale do Mucuri, Norte de Minas, Triângulo Mineiro, Alto Paranaíba e Noroeste de Minas (veja lista completa de cidades abaixo) .

articles.title: Estudante que perdeu bolsa do por vício da mãe em apostas presta Enem | G1
articles.standfirst: Em agosto, o g1 contou a história do estudante que ainda tentava reverter a situação da bolsa e começar a cursar Psicologia em uma unidade da UNIP, em São Paulo.
articles.summary: Em agosto, o g1 contou a história do estudante que ainda tentava reverter a situação da bolsa e começar a cursar Psicologia em uma unidade da UNIP, em São Paulo.
articles.body:
Estudante Eduardo dos Santos tem bolsa do Prouni indeferida. — Foto: Reprodução

Depois de ter uma bolsa integral pelo Programa Universidade para Todos (Prouni) negada por conta das movimentações financeiras de sua mãe relacionadas a plataformas de aposta online, Eduardo Luvizetto dos Santos decidiu prestar o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio ( Enem) pela terceira vez .

➡️Ele é um dos mais de cinco milhões de inscritos que devem realizar o segundo dia de provas do Enem neste domingo (15).

Em agosto, o g1 contou a história do estudante que ainda tentava reverter a situação da bolsa e começar a cursar Psicologia em uma unidade da UNIP, em São Paulo. (relembre a história abaixo)

Apesar dos esforços, inclusive judiciais, Eduardo não conseguiu garantir a inclusão no Prouni e a solução foi tentar uma vaga na universidade realizando o Enem mais uma vez.

"Foi muito difícil, depois de passar por tudo isso, me dar conta que teria que tentar de novo. [...] Mas percebi que não tinha o que fazer, eu precisava tentar de novo. Se eu consegui uma vez, posso conseguir de novo", reflete.

Eduardo conta que todo o processo até cair em si de que a situação da bolsa era irreversível e que ele teria que buscar uma nova vaga foi algo que lhe gerou muita ansiedade.

Segundo o estudante, só semanas após a repercussão do caso foi possível entender que o caminho seria voltar a estudar para prestar o Enem novamente.

"Confesso que a situação afetou totalmente os meus estudos, minha motivação, minha dedicação. Eu tinha entrado já na universidade e depois foi como se tivesse perdido tudo", lembra.

Ele explica que, apesar da decepção e da carga emocional e psicológica com que teve que lidar ao longo dos últimos meses, se sentiu tranquilo no primeiro dia de prova.

Além de ter a intenção de usar a nota do Enem para estudar Psicologia, ele agora também tem a ideia de tentar uma vaga em um curso de Administração Pública.

"Resiliência a gente cria desde quando a gente nasce, vindo da periferia. Mesmo com tudo o que aconteceu eu pensei 'não posso abandonar tudo agora'", relata o estudante.

Ainda que atendesse a todos os requisitos educacionais exigidos pelo Prouni e tivesse renda mensal familiar de até 1,5 salário mínimo por pessoa, Luvizetto teve a bolsa negada por conta de movimentações financeiras de sua mãe em plataformas de aposta.

A justificativa da negativa da bolsa foi que a renda superava o aceito pelo programa, justamente algo decorrente a ganhos de um parente próximo.

👉 O Programa Universidade para Todos é uma iniciativa do governo federal que oferece bolsas integrais (100%) e parciais (50% de desconto) em instituições de ensino particulares.

Na época, a UNIP afirmou que havia uma grande entrada de valores, de forma constante, vinculada a jogos virtuais de apostas nos documentos entregues pelo candidato e que, por lei, "prêmios são considerados renda".

O estudante chegou a argumentar junto à universidade que "jogo online não é renda" e que sua mãe enfrentava uma condição conhecida como ludopatia .

🎲 A ludopatia é uma condição médica caracterizada pelo desejo incontrolável de continuar jogando . A doença é reconhecida pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) e no Brasil engloba quadros como mania de jogo e apostas e jogo patológico.

Uma das grandes conquistas com a repercussão do caso foi justamente o acompanhamento psicológico da mãe.

Eduardo conta que ela parou de apostar desde que a bolsa do filho foi impactada pelas movimentações financeiras e passou a tratar o quadro realmente como doença.

"A gente conseguiu uma psicóloga através da página que tenho no Instagram, que inclusive faz doutorado na UFMG estudando sobre vícios. E minha mãe está gostando muito do tratamento", comemora.

articles.standfirst: Com barracas inundadas e sem roupas adequadas, milhares de crianças, grávidas e bebês palestinos enfrentam condições precárias, enquanto impasse entre Israel e Hamas trava reconstrução de Gaza e chegada de ajuda.
articles.summary: Com barracas inundadas e sem roupas adequadas, milhares de crianças, grávidas e bebês palestinos enfrentam condições precárias, enquanto impasse entre Israel e Hamas trava reconstrução de Gaza e chegada de ajuda.
articles.body:
Menino palestino é visto em acampamento alagado na Cidade de Gaza. — Foto: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters

As fortes chuvas e a queda das temperaturas neste outono no hemisfério norte estão agravando a situação humanitária dos civis na Faixa de Gaza.

As chuvas torrenciais do último fim de semana mataram pelo menos seis pessoas , incluindo crianças, segundo o Fundo das Nações Unidas para a Infância (Unicef). Autoridades locais informaram que pelo menos 70 mil barracas foram inundadas e mais de 200 mil pessoas foram afetadas .

"Nos últimos dois dias, temos tentado firmar nossa barraca com areia e entulho para impedir a entrada de água", disse à DW, por telefone, Rawan Al-Omari, mãe de dois filhos.

Ela e os filhos dividem uma barraca a oeste de Jabalia, no norte de Gaza. "Toda a área ao nosso redor virou lama, então até sair da barraca ficou difícil", afirmou a mulher de 33 anos. "Tudo é exaustivo".

A chuva também encharcou a tenda e todos os pertences de Radi Amin, de 45 anos, e de seus três filhos.

"Durante três dias seguidos, tentamos secar nossas roupas enquanto meus filhos tremiam de frio", contou à DW. "Só na quarta-feira, quando o sol finalmente apareceu e esquentou o suficiente, nossos pertences começaram a secar".

Segundo Amin, "as fortes chuvas serviram como um lembrete contundente da situação realmente desesperadora" em que eles vivem.

Tendas são vistas alagadas após forte chuva na Cidade de Gaza — Foto: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters

Enquanto isso, equipes humanitárias começaram a desobstruir tubulações de esgoto e bacias de captação de águas pluviais em 60 locais, o que vai auxiliar cerca de 30 mil famílias, informou na quarta-feira (11) o Escritório das Nações Unidas para a Coordenação de Assuntos Humanitários (OCHA).

No entanto, organizações parceiras do OCHA alertaram que não há espaço suficiente para realocar as pessoas que vivem em áreas inundadas ou em edifícios danificados pela guerra .

"As autoridades israelenses estão restringindo o acesso dos palestinos a qualquer área além da chamada 'Linha Amarela', o que significa que a maior parte do território de Gaza permanece inacessível", afirmou o OCHA.

A guerra na Faixa de Gaza, desencadeada após os ataques terroristas do grupo terrorista Hamas contra Israel em 7de outubro de 2023, destruiu a maior parte da infraestrutura e das moradias do território.

Mais de 74.600 pessoas foram mortas na Faixa de Gaza , segundo dados do Ministério da Saúde de Gaza, controlado pelo Hamas. O número não faz distinção entre combatentes e civis.

Israel controla cerca de dois terços do território, delimitados por uma linha de demarcação militar, a chamada Linha Amarela .

O Hamas continua exercendo o poder em grande parte do território restante, próximo ao mar Mediterrâneo, onde vive a maioria dos cerca de 2 milhões de habitantes de Gaza . A maior parte deles foi deslocada várias vezes e vive em barracas, acampamentos ou casas consideradas inseguras.

➡️ O Hamas é classificado como organização terrorista pela Alemanha, pela União Europeia, pelos Estados Unidos e por outros países.

Como parte do cessar-fogo de outubro de 2025, mediado pelos Estados Unidos, o presidente Donald Trump criou o Conselho de Paz para supervisionar a implementação do acordo, bem como a governança e a reconstrução de Gaza no pós-guerra.

Segundo uma avaliação conjunta do Banco Mundial, das Nações Unidas e da União Europeia, publicada em abril de 2026, a recuperação e a reconstrução de Gaza exigirão cerca de US$ 71,4 bilhões (cerca de R$ 402 bilhões) ao longo da próxima década.

No entanto, houve poucos avanços. Os negociadores não têm conseguido chegar a um acordo sobre as condições para o desarmamento do Hamas e a retirada das tropas israelenses do território.

Apesar do cessar-fogo, Israel continua realizando ataques aéreos contra Gaza. Nesta última quinta (12), os israelenses atacaram o Hospital Nasser, em Khan Younis, matando seis pessoas e alegando ter como alvo supostos integrantes do Hamas.

Para Nathan Brown, professor de ciência política e relações internacionais da Universidade George Washington, nos Estados Unidos, as chuvas atuais exemplificam o impasse do plano de paz de Trump para Gaza.

"A incapacidade do Conselho de Paz de fazer a reconstrução avançar, ou mesmo de garantir assistência humanitária de forma confiável, deve-se fundamentalmente às objeções israelenses, baseadas na exigência de que o Hamas se desarme completamente primeiro", disse à DW.

Até as recentes eleições em Israel, o Conselho de Paz demonstrava pouco interesse em contestar essa posição, acrescentou Brown: "Agora, está disposto a se manifestar publicamente, embora sem adotar um tom muito confrontador".

Medidas tomadas por Israel são insuficientes

Palestino enfrenta alagamento em acampamento durante um dia chuvoso na Cidade de Gaza, 7 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters

Na segunda-feira, o Conselho de Paz divulgou uma declaração afirmando que as medidas tomadas por Israel para melhorar a situação humanitária antes da chegada do inverno no hemisfério norte continuam insuficientes.

"Pedimos à liderança do atual governo de Israel que aja imediatamente para autorizar e facilitar a entrada de todos os suprimentos necessários para enfrentar o inverno e prestar assistência humanitária".

A Coordenação das Atividades do Governo de Israel nos Territórios (COGAT) informou, no mesmo dia, que, entre outros equipamentos, 12 caminhões de sucção de esgoto destinados ao Comitê Internacional da Cruz Vermelha haviam chegado a Gaza e que 91 mil barracas e mais de 8.200 caminhões com lonas, cobertores e roupas de inverno haviam entrado no território nos últimos meses.

Em sua declaração, o Conselho de Paz também pediu que o Hamas cumprisse os compromissos assumidos no cessar-fogo, incluindo depor as armas e transferir o poder de governo. O Hamas rejeitou as críticas em um comunicado e acusou Israel de obstruir a implementação do plano de paz e impedir a entrada de suprimentos humanitários urgentemente necessários.

As Nações Unidas e diversas organizações internacionais acusaram Israel de impedir sistematicamente a entrada de abrigos pré-fabricados em Gaza. A ONU afirmou que cerca de 150 mil barracas estavam fora de Gaza, prontas para serem enviadas, aguardando as autorizações necessárias — alegação rejeitada por Israel.

O primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu, que permanece à frente de um governo interino enquanto um novo governo tenta ser formado após as eleições de 27 de outubro, negou que Israel fosse responsável pela deterioração das condições e atribuiu a culpa ao Hamas.

Ele advertiu que, "enquanto o Hamas permanecer no poder, usará todos os itens de uso civil e militar que entrarem em Gaza para consolidar seu regime de terror e ampliar seu arsenal militar”.

Suprimentos atendem a menos de 1% das necessidades

Palestinos deslocados pela guerra enfrentam fortes chuvas enquanto vivem em tentas em acampamento na Cidade de Gaza — Foto: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters

Para a população de Gaza, esse impasse, em meio à aproximação do inverno, significa a continuidade das dificuldades.

"Crianças e famílias enfrentam condições devastadoras, com cerca de 1,2 milhão de pessoas, incluindo mais de 560 mil crianças, vivendo em condições de abrigo críticas ou catastróficas", disse à DW Ahmad Alhendawi, diretor regional da organização humanitária Save the Children.

A quantidade de roupas de inverno disponíveis em Gaza continua muito abaixo do necessário, acrescentou.

"Como os suprimentos disponíveis atendem a menos de 1% das necessidades, centenas de milhares de crianças enfrentam o inverno sem roupas, cobertores ou aquecimento adequados, ficando expostas à hipotermia e a doenças respiratórias", afirmou Alhendawi.

Além disso, Nestor Owomuhangi, representante do Fundo de População das Nações Unidas (UNFPA) nos Territórios Palestinos, disse à DW que cerca de 400 mil pessoas em Gaza continuam vivendo em áreas com alto risco de inundação, incluindo aproximadamente 10 mil gestantes .

"Para mulheres e meninas que já enfrentam deslocamento forçado e fome, a chuva ameaça sua saúde, segurança e dignidade”, afirmou à DW, acrescentando que, "com cerca de 180 bebês nascendo todos os dias, mães e recém-nascidos precisam urgentemente de abrigos secos e aquecidos".

articles.title: UnB inaugura 1º placa de projeto que mapeia locais de memória da ditadura; DF tem 12 pontos na lista | G1
articles.standfirst: Teatro de Arena Honestino Guimarães recebeu sinalização nesta quinta. Iniciativa prevê marcos em todo o país para preservar memória da repressão e da resistência ao regime.
articles.summary: Teatro de Arena Honestino Guimarães recebeu sinalização nesta quinta. Iniciativa prevê marcos em todo o país para preservar memória da repressão e da resistência ao regime.
articles.body:
Mais de 300 locais históricos relacionados à repressão e à resistência durante a ditadura militar já foram identificados em diferentes regiões do Brasil.

A iniciativa faz parte do projeto Lugares pela Memória , do Ministério dos Direitos Humanos e da Cidadania (MDHC), que busca reconhecer esses espaços e preservar a história das violações de direitos humanos no país.

O Teatro de Arena Honestino Guimarães, da Universidade de Brasília ( UnB ), foi escolhido para receber a primeira placa de sinalização do projeto no país . A cerimônia ocorreu nesta quinta-feira (12).

A escolha da UnB levou em consideração a relevância histórica da universidade. Durante a inauguração da placa, a ministra dos Direitos Humanos e da Cidadania, Janine Mello dos Santos, afirmou que a placa representa o início de um percurso nacional de identificação e sinalização desses espaços.

“Essa é a primeira placa de sinalização de muitas que ainda virão nos próximos meses. Ela representa muito mais do que a identificação de um espaço físico. Representa o reconhecimento público de que determinados lugares guardam histórias que não podem ser esquecidas. Lugares onde o Estado violou direitos, perseguiu, prendeu, torturou e fez desaparecer pessoas , mas também lugares onde mulheres e homens resistiram, se organizaram e lutaram para que a democracia pudesse existir”, disse.

UnB inaugura primeira placa de projeto que identifica locais de memória da ditadura militar. — Foto: Duda Rodrigues/MDHC

Entre os próximos locais que deverão receber placas estão:

o Centro de Documentação e Memória da Universidade Estadual Paulista (CEDEM/ Unesp );

o Sindicato dos Metalúrgicos do ABC, em São Paulo;

o Memorial da Luta pela Justiça, iniciativa vinculada à Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil em São Paulo (OAB-SP);

o Núcleo Memória, na Pontifícia Universidade Católica de São Paulo (PUC-SP).

"Cada placa que instalarmos a partir de agora será uma ponte entre passado e futuro, para que não se esqueça, para que nunca mais aconteça e para que saibamos o que passamos para sermos o país que nós somos hoje", completou a ministra.

Chefe da Assessoria Especial de Defesa da Democracia, Memória e Verdade do MDHC, Hamilton Pereira afirmou que o projeto busca recuperar histórias que não podem ser esquecidas e aproximar a sociedade da própria trajetória .

“O que nós temos aqui hoje é o início de um projeto, a materialização dele, que busca voltar o olhar para trás, para integrar, não para esquecer, nem para apagar jamais a trajetória dessa gente teimosa que é o povo brasileiro. Nós precisamos integrar os anos de sombra para que a gente se aproxime da verdadeira face do país”, afirmou.

Construído no início da década de 1970, durante a ditadura militar, o Teatro de Arena Honestino Guimarães se tornou um dos espaços de mobilização política e cultural da Universidade de Brasília.

Movimento estudantil no Teatro Arena da UnB durante assembleia-greve Fora Azevedo, 1980 — Foto: Divulgação/Acervo ACE UnB

O local recebeu assembleias estudantis, debates e apresentações artísticas. Em 1997, o espaço recebeu o nome de Honestino Guimarães, em homenagem ao líder estudantil e ex-aluno de Geologia da UnB, desaparecido em 1973 durante a repressão política.

Durante a cerimônia, a reitora da UnB, Rozana Naves, afirmou que a repressão atingiu a universidade desde os primeiros anos de funcionamento e interferiu na liberdade acadêmica. Assista:

“A repressão não ocorreu à margem da vida desta universidade. Ela alcançou os seus primeiros anos, interferiu na liberdade acadêmica e atingiu aqueles que se opuseram à violência do regime. Este lugar reúne a memória do autoritarismo e a determinação das gerações que a ele resistiram”, afirmou.

A reitora lembrou que a universidade sofreu intervenções, invasões policiais e militares, perseguições, prisões, afastamentos e expulsões de professores. Estudantes também foram impedidos de continuar os estudos.

Rozana citou vítimas da repressão que passaram pela instituição – Honestino Guimarães, Iêda Santos Delgado e Paulo de Tarso Celestino, estudantes da UnB que foram vítimas de desaparecimento forçado durante a ditadura.

A coordenadora do Diretório Central dos Estudantes (DCE) Honestino Guimarães, Alice Paulino, também participou da cerimônia. Alice contou que veio de Planaltina e que, durante a formação, nem sempre teve contato com a história de pessoas que participaram dos movimentos de resistência e foram perseguidas pelo regime.

“Eu vim de um lugar em que a ditadura, por exemplo, não era uma realidade muito palpável para mim. Talvez até minha família não conheça o nome de pessoas que fizeram parte desse movimento, que foram perseguidas e torturadas. Me emociona muito finalmente ter um espaço com tantas pessoas que realmente prezam por essa história e por esses nomes”, afirmou.

“É muito importante que estejamos aqui justamente para que aqueles que foram silenciados não sejam silenciados novamente e que a história nunca seja esquecida”, completou.

A coordenadora do Diretório Central dos Estudantes (DCE) Honestino Guimarães, Alice Paulino. — Foto: Duda Rodrigues/MDHC

O Observatório Nacional dos Direitos Humanos (ObservaDH) atualizou, durante esta semana, o mapeamento dos lugares de memória em Brasília. A lista passou a reunir 12 espaços:

Universidade de Brasília (UnB) – Teatro de Arena;

Destacamento de Operações de Informações – Centro de Operações de Defesa Interna (DOI-Codi);

Sede do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico (BNDE) / Departamento Geral de Investigação e DOPS – Polícia Federal.

Pelotão de Investigações Criminais (PIC).

O levantamento reúne locais relacionados às violações de direitos humanos e às experiências de resistência durante o regime militar.

A metodologia utiliza informações investigadas pela Comissão Nacional da Verdade , por comissões estaduais, municipais e universitárias da verdade, além de pesquisas acadêmicas e outras iniciativas institucionais.

O mapa interativo está disponível no Observatório Nacional dos Direitos Humanos, plataforma pública do ministério. O levantamento continua em andamento e recebe atualizações com a identificação de novos espaços.

articles.title: Belle Daltro: Humor, autenticidade e milhões de seguidores nas redes | G1
articles.standfirst: Baiana conquistou uma legião de fãs com vídeos de humor, linguagem espontânea e referências à cultura popular. Em 2026, ganhou ainda mais visibilidade ao se posicionar durante as eleições e participar da cobertura do Afropunk Bahia.
articles.summary: Baiana conquistou uma legião de fãs com vídeos de humor e referências à cultura popular. Em 2026, ganhou mais visibilidade ao se posicionar durante as eleições.
articles.body:
Com um jeito espontâneo de falar, expressões típicas da Bahia e vídeos que retratam situações do cotidiano, a influenciadora digital Belle Daltro conquistou milhões de seguidores e se tornou um dos nomes de destaque do humor nas redes sociais. Nascida em Salvador , ela ultrapassou a marca de 6 milhões de seguidores apenas no Instagram e vem ampliando sua presença para além da internet.

Por trás do nome artístico, está Isabelle Santos Daltro, que cresceu na periferia da capital baiana e transformou as próprias vivências em uma das principais características do conteúdo que produz.

Entre brincadeiras, comentários sobre relacionamentos e histórias pessoais, a influenciadora construiu uma relação de proximidade com o público.

Irmã do também influenciador Cristian Bell, conhecido nacionalmente pelos vídeos de humor, Belle começou a ganhar espaço nas redes sociais em 2022. Apesar da ligação familiar com um nome já consolidado na internet, a baiana desenvolveu um estilo próprio e passou a reunir uma audiência de milhões de pessoas.

Belle Daltro acumula 6 milhões de seguidores apenas em uma rede social — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O crescimento também fez com que Belle ultrapassasse os limites do entretenimento. Durante as eleições presidenciais de 2026, a influenciadora ganhou repercussão ao se posicionar, utilizando as redes sociais para discutir questões políticas e incentivar a participação dos jovens na votação.

A exposição colocou a baiana no centro de discussões nas plataformas digitais e ampliou a visibilidade de uma trajetória que começou com vídeos de humor e passou a incluir posicionamentos sobre questões sociais.

Das comunidades de Salvador para a internet

A origem periférica é uma parte importante da história de Belle Daltro, já que, antes de alcançar milhões de pessoas, a influenciadora viveu uma realidade distante da fama, marcada por dificuldades financeiras que ela própria já relatou publicamente.

A relação com a comunidade onde cresceu também aparece na maneira como se comunica. Sem abandonar o sotaque, as gírias e as expressões populares de Salvador, Belle faz da identidade baiana uma marca dos vídeos que publica.

A produção de conteúdo começou a ganhar força em 2022, quando passou a compartilhar publicações com mais frequência. Os vídeos misturam humor, situações familiares, relacionamentos e acontecimentos do dia a dia.

A presença de Cristian Bell também faz parte dessa trajetória, porque os irmãos compartilham o gosto pelo humor e já apareceram juntos em conteúdos que repercutiram na internet.

Com o passar dos anos, Belle deixou de ser reconhecida apenas como irmã do influenciador, que já tinha uma trajetória consolidada no mercado de influência, e conquistou espaço próprio nas plataformas digitais.

A popularidade de Belle também abriu portas para participações em projetos de entretenimento e coberturas de grandes eventos.

Em 2024, Belle participou do Rancho do Maia , reality idealizado pelo influenciador Carlinhos Maia, que reúne personalidades da internet em uma programação marcada por convivência, desafios e produção de conteúdo. A participação ajudou a apresentar a baiana a públicos de outras regiões do país, que torcem pela presença dela em outros programas.

Recentemente, Belle ganhou destaque durante o Afropunk Bahia 2026 , realizado em Salvador, nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro. A influenciadora foi escolhida para atuar como repórter das redes sociais da TV Globo durante o festival, que reúne artistas nacionais e internacionais e celebra a cultura negra.

Na cobertura, Belle levou para as entrevistas e os bastidores do evento o mesmo estilo descontraído que utiliza nas próprias redes sociais. Três vídeos produzidos em colaboração com a Globo ultrapassaram, juntos, 4 milhões de visualizações, além de somarem mais de 220 mil curtidas e quase 9 mil comentários.

Na quarta-feira (11), Belle Daltro também participou do Jornal da Manhã e do Bahia Meio Dia, telejornais da TV Bahia. As aparições na televisão reforçam a presença da influenciadora em diferentes espaços de comunicação, após conquistar milhões de seguidores com os conteúdos publicados nas redes sociais.

Além do humor e dos trabalhos profissionais, Belle compartilha momentos da vida pessoal com os seguidores — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Além do humor e dos trabalhos profissionais, Belle compartilha momentos da vida pessoal com os seguidores.

A influenciadora mantém um relacionamento com Amanda Lago, com quem divide registros da rotina e experiências nas redes sociais. As duas ficaram noivas em abril de 2024, após quatro anos de relacionamento.

Em janeiro de 2025, Belle emocionou seguidores ao anunciar a conquista de uma casa ao lado da companheira. Na ocasião, relembrou as origens das duas: ela, da região da Liberdade, e Amanda, de Periperi, no Subúrbio de Salvador.

A conquista foi apresentada como a realização de um sonho que parecia distante da realidade vivida pelas mulheres anos antes.

articles.title: Como preparar seu filho para um mundo em transformação? | G1
articles.standfirst: Com chegada a Uberlândia em 2027, a RED HOUSE conecta educação internacional bilíngue, autonomia e desenvolvimento socioemocional.
articles.summary: Com chegada a Uberlândia em 2027, a RED HOUSE conecta educação internacional bilíngue, autonomia e desenvolvimento socioemocional.
articles.body:
Atividade pedagógica em unidade da rede — Foto: Divulgação Red House

Escolher uma escola é também pensar nas possibilidades que uma criança terá para descobrir seus interesses, construir relações e encontrar seu lugar no mundo. Em meio às mudanças tecnológicas e às novas formas de trabalhar e se comunicar, uma pergunta ganha importância para as famílias: quais conhecimentos e habilidades ajudarão os filhos a enfrentar situações que ainda nem conseguimos prever?

O relatório Future of Jobs 2025, do Fórum Econômico Mundial, ajuda a dimensionar essa transformação. Segundo os empregadores consultados, 39% das competências atuais dos trabalhadores deverão mudar ou se tornar desatualizadas até 2030. Ao lado dos conhecimentos tecnológicos, o estudo destaca a importância do pensamento criativo, da resiliência, da flexibilidade e da aprendizagem contínua.

Esse cenário amplia a discussão sobre o papel da escola. Além de aprender conteúdos, os estudantes precisam de oportunidades para investigar, fazer escolhas, colaborar e aplicar o conhecimento em diferentes situações. É com essa perspectiva que a RED HOUSE International School prepara sua chegada a Uberlândia, com início das aulas previsto para 2027.

Referência em educação internacional bilíngue no Brasil, a RED HOUSE tem 18 unidades em 8 Estados, com presença em cidades como São Paulo, Curitiba, Recife, Cuiabá, Goiânia e Campo Grande.

Uberlândia será a segunda unidade da rede em Minas Gerais, que também prepara a abertura de um campus em Belo Horizonte para o ano letivo de 2027. Na cidade, a escola está instalada na Avenida Vinhedos, 1341, na zona Sul.

A RED HOUSE de São Paulo integra a seleção “As Escolas Mais Premium do Brasil 2025/26”, publicada pela Forbes. A rede reúne uma proposta educacional internacional, metodologia própria de aquisição de linguagem e uma equipe dedicada ao desenvolvimento curricular. “A nossa chegada a Uberlândia reforça o compromisso de oferecer às famílias mineiras uma proposta pedagógica que forma alunos com mentalidade internacional, sem perder a conexão com a cultura e os valores brasileiros”, afirma Michel Lam, fundador da RED HOUSE.

A proposta da RED HOUSE conecta aprendizagem em dois idiomas ao desenvolvimento acadêmico, social e emocional. — Foto: Divulgação Red House

O que muda quando se aprende em dois idiomas?

Na proposta da RED HOUSE, o inglês faz parte da aprendizagem dos conteúdos curriculares. A imersão diária no idioma permite que os estudantes o utilizem de forma natural para compreender assuntos, participar de atividades e expressar ideias.

Português e inglês se complementam na formação. A identidade brasileira permanece presente no currículo, alinhado à Base Nacional Comum Curricular, com valorização da literatura e da cultura do país.

A dimensão internacional aparece também na maneira de abordar o conhecimento. Questões mundiais se conectam a temas nacionais e locais, incentivando os estudantes a compreender diferentes perspectivas e a relacioná-las à própria realidade.

Para as famílias, essa proposta representa a possibilidade de oferecer aos filhos uma formação em que a comunicação em dois idiomas acompanha a ampliação do repertório cultural e das formas de aprender.

Como uma criança aprende a tomar decisões? Como desenvolve confiança para apresentar uma ideia, rever uma hipótese ou tentar novamente? Essas questões fazem parte da proposta pedagógica da RED HOUSE. Seis pilares orientam o trabalho com o perfil do aluno, a capacidade de escolher e agir, a organização do currículo, a aprendizagem ligada a situações reais, a avaliação contínua e a integração entre áreas do conhecimento.

A intenção é criar oportunidades para que os estudantes participem ativamente da aprendizagem. Investigar uma pergunta, discutir possibilidades e colocar conhecimentos em prática são caminhos para desenvolver autonomia com acompanhamento dos educadores.

O currículo conta com o trabalho do RED Lab (Research in Education Design), núcleo exclusivo que reúne pesquisadores e especialistas responsáveis por desenvolver e atualizar metodologias, processos e conteúdos educacionais.

Em Uberlândia, o projeto ocupa um terreno de aproximadamente 7.500 m². Arquitetos e educadores trabalharam juntos na concepção dos ambientes, com espaços para atividades pedagógicas, esporte e convivência.

A estrutura prevê quadra poliesportiva coberta, quadras de areia, pista de atletismo, campo de futebol gramado e playgrounds. As áreas externas também poderão receber atividades de aprendizagem em espaços arborizados.

Para a Educação Infantil, estão previstos fluxo independente e playground exclusivo, além de refeitórios segmentados por faixa etária no complexo.

A conclusão das obras está prevista para janeiro de 2027.

Perspectiva ilustrativa do campus de Uberlândia, com ambientes planejados para integrar aprendizagem, esporte e convivência. — Foto: Divulgação Red House

As famílias com filhos na Red House Uberlândia escolhem o modelo premium de educação. A unidade Uberlândia pretende fazer parte em breve, do seleto grupo de escolas premium certificadas pelo International Baccalaureate (IB), currículo educacional global de alta excelência acadêmica, criado em 1968 na Suíça, voltado para formar estudantes críticos, autônomos e com mentalidade internacional.

A escolha de uma escola envolve entender como o projeto pedagógico se traduz na rotina e como poderá acompanhar cada etapa do desenvolvimento da criança.

As famílias interessadas na RED HOUSE Uberlândia podem agendar uma reunião para conhecer a proposta, conversar com a equipe e consultar as turmas disponíveis para 2027.

articles.title: New Orleans port seeks tanker seizure after cruise ship crash sparks $1M lawsuit
articles.summary: A federal lawsuit seeks more than $1 million for damage to a New Orleans port terminal after an asphalt tanker collided with a river cruise ship on the Missi...
articles.body:
The Port of New Orleans is seeking more than $1 million in damages after an asphalt tanker struck a docked river cruise ship on the Mississippi River, with a federal judge authorizing the tanker's seizure.

The lawsuit, filed Friday in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana and obtained by FOX Business, names the Atlantic Asphalt tanker, its owner, Nave Shipping SA, and its management company, Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd.

The port alleges the collision caused more than $1 million in physical damage to its Thalia Street Terminal, where the American Heritage cruise ship was docked Friday afternoon.

The port is also seeking compensation for cleanup, repairs and potential business interruption and lost revenue.

The complaint accuses the tanker and the companies responsible for its operation of negligence, alleging they failed to take adequate precautions to avoid the collision.

Chief U.S. District Judge Wendy Vitter granted the port's emergency request Friday, finding that circumstances warranted the vessel's prompt arrest. The court issued a warrant authorizing the tanker's seizure, although it was not immediately clear whether the warrant had been executed.

The port is also seeking the tanker's potential sale to satisfy its financial claims. No sale has been ordered.

The collision occurred around 12:30 p.m. Friday near the Crescent City Connection bridge in New Orleans. The tanker appeared to lose steering control before striking the American Heritage, causing the cruise ship to capsize and partially sink.

Thirty-two people were taken to hospitals, but no fatalities or critical injuries were reported.

In a statement Saturday, OSM Thome said the tanker was stable at anchor and that the company was cooperating with authorities investigating the collision.

Representatives for the Port of New Orleans, OSM Thome, American Cruise Lines and the U.S. Coast Guard for comment did not immediately respond to FOX Business' requests for comment.

articles.title: Pope Leo speaks on community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes
articles.summary: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.
articles.body:
On a visit to an isolated Andean village in his former diocese, Pope Leo XIV has spoken about the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future", which he said had left communities under threat.

About 6,000 people live in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, which is located in a remote part of the Andes mountains in northern Peru, but the Pope's visit drew a crowd of about 20,000, according to the Vatican.

At an outdoor Mass, Pope Leo spoke of "declining birth rates that are emptying villages," and the unequal distribution of the land's resources.

Over 40% of the population in the Cajamarca region, where the town is located, live in poverty - the highest figure in Peru, according to official data.

Cajamarca has lost the highest number of people to internal migration, with 729,000 people born there now living elsewhere in Peru.

In his sermon, Pope Leo thanked those who had made the journey to him and emphasised the importance of never losing heart, despite life's difficulties.

Santa Cruz is within the Diocese of Chiclayo, where Pope Leo served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. During his tenure, he visited Santa Cruz several times a year to minister to the town's rural population.

On Saturday he returned by helicopter, where he was greeted by singing and cheering. He later did a tour in a popemobile, where he waved to people who had travelled from across the region to see him.

Speaking at a local parish on Saturday, the Pope said he felt "joy" at being able to visit the small town once again.

"It is like a very big dream that the Lord has allowed this servant to come here," he said.

Rev. Kevin Noriega, who was ordained in 2018 by the then-bishop, told Reuters the visit had brought "enormous hope and emotion" to Santa Cruz.

He said: "People are eager to experience this Holy Mass ... because after so much time they will be able to see their bishop - 'Father Robert,' as they used to call him - now as the Holy Father."

Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the leader of the Catholic church, who was elected in May 2025.

The 12-day trip has included stops in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in Peru carries personal significance.

The US-born pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

The pontiff is set to leave Chiclayo on Sunday, when he will head to Cusco, and then on to a Peruvian sector of the Amazon rainforest. His tour of the region will conclude on Monday, at which point Pope Leo will return to Rome.

articles.title: US judge halts Trump's plan to close historic DC golf course for redevelopment
articles.summary: A US judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's plan to shut down a historic public golf course in Washington for a 15-month redevelopment, ruling
articles.body: A US judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's plan to shut down a historic public golf course in Washington for a 15-month redevelopment, ruling that the government cannot close the park to the public while a legal challenge against the project is pending.US District Judge Ana Reyes, in a 30-page order issued on Saturday, said the administration was seeking to close a historic public space that was regularly used by Washington residents. "The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," she wrote, as quoted by Reuters.Reyes said the administration's stated reasons for shutting the site were "pretextual" and that the government had violated at least two federal laws to meet what she described as an "arbitrary deadline". The order prevents the government from closing East Potomac Park and its golf course during the hours they were open as of November 14. It will remain in force until November 28 or until further orders from the court.The golf course has historical significance. Opened in 1920, it was among Washington's earliest public golf courses and also became a site of the city's civil rights struggle. In 1941, three Black golfers challenged racial segregation at the course and played under police protection, helping advance the integration of public recreational facilities in the capital. The National Park Service recognises it as part of the historic East and West Potomac Parks district.The ruling came a day before the planned closure of East Potomac Park, located along the Potomac River, about two miles from the White House. The administration had announced that work would begin on November 15, with the golf course expected to remain shut for 15 months.The legal challenge was brought by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers, who argued that the redevelopment would fundamentally change the character of the accessible public course and make it unaffordable for ordinary residents. They also warned that closing the park and beginning construction would cause irreparable harm to the public.Trump's own social media announcements about the planned closure also weighed on the judge's decision. In an October 26 post, the president said the course would shut as scheduled on November 15 for renovation and rebuilding, citing competition, safety, modernisation and aesthetic improvements.The proposed overhaul would replace the park's existing 36 holes across three golf courses with a single 18-hole championship-level course. Trump has said the redevelopment would create a "World Championship Public Facility" capable of hosting major tournaments such as the US Open and Ryder Cup, while remaining accessible to the public.The Justice Department said the ruling did not prevent the administration from continuing to plan the redevelopment. It also maintained that the National Park Service could restrict access to facilities where public safety was at risk.Trump criticised the ruling in a social media post on Saturday, claiming that Reyes did not want the administration to "quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course". He also said Washington-area residents would receive a 50 per cent discount on all rates at the redeveloped facility.The case has seen repeated clashes between Reyes and the administration. The judge had earlier blocked the National Park Service from cutting down trees or making other irreversible changes to the park without advance notice. She also raised concerns over the administration's removal of hundreds of trees without adequately informing the plaintiffs.Reyes has also initiated an examination into whether Interior Department and National Park Service officials, as well as Justice Department lawyers, misled the court or violated ethical rules during the proceedings. The Justice Department had sought her removal from the case, questioning her impartiality, but she declined to recuse herself.The golf course redevelopment is part of Trump's broader effort to reshape Washington through major construction projects, including a proposed triumphal arch and a new White House ballroom.You use AI every day. articles.title: When Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang, in a closed-door meeting with more than 30 company executives, reportedly told a senior VP: I hope you die and put us all ...
articles.summary: Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang was a good or a bad leader? The reviews are mixed.
articles.body: Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang was a good or a bad leader? The reviews are mixed. While there are online petitions reportedly signed by 5,000-plus employees asking for his reinstatement, there are also some who see his exit as a breather. According to a report in New York Post, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang routinely subjected employees to harsh verbal abuse and once even threw a water bottle at a senior executive during an outburst at the office.Despite cultivating a laid-back public persona marked by his signature black leather jackets and stories about his early years washing dishes and cleaning toilets, Huang presided over a tense internal environment where employees feared his temper during marathon meetings, insiders told the Post. As per the New York Post report, the 63-year-old former Nvidia CEO maintained an unusual corporate structure in which more than 60 top leaders reported directly to him.In one incident, the report states, during a closed-door meeting last February with over 30 executives in attendance, Huang reportedly directed his anger at Jay Puri, who was then serving as executive vice president of worldwide field operations. According to a source familiar with the exchange, Huang told Puri, “I hope you get the flu and I hope it gets worse,” before adding, “I hope you die and put us all out of our misery.” A source told the Post that while yelling was common for Huang, that specific remark left the room stunned and silent.'Jensen Huang does not like disagreement'The confrontation was part of a broader pattern of behavior, sources told the publication, noting that some employees were surprised his outbursts had not leaked prior to his departure. During a three-hour meeting in 2025 with roughly 40 staffers present, Huang allegedly told a senior sales leader, “You don’t know dick about my business.” On another occasion, he reportedly kicked a senior leader out of a meeting—the executive’s first with Huang—after shouting, “Are you smirking at me? I see nothing but dead faces … Get out!” Insiders also recounted an incident at Nvidia’s Santa Clara, California, headquarters in which Huang allegedly hurled a water bottle at a top executive during a meeting.Huang’s abrasive approach extended beyond internal staff, according to the Post. In a New York Times article published this week, The Thinking Machine biographer Stephen Witt wrote that Huang’s humble public demeanor served “to cloak his arrogance,” stating that contradicting him on even trivial matters “was like lighting a fuse” that led to him screaming at employees for their “idiocy.” Additionally, the Post noted a report in which Huang lectured a group of cloud computing CEOs at a conference in Berlin, sharing a story about a Japanese soup vendor who refused to sell him a second bowl so he would not run out for other waiting customers. Huang reportedly told the executives, “He’s a better businessperson than all of you,” and accused them of failing to establish the value of Nvidia’s products.Jensen Huang's resignation over 'spy affair'The accounts of Huang’s workplace conduct follow his resignation earlier this week, which came after he admitted to an affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who is not related to him. According to reports cited by the Post, Huang allegedly had affairs with at least three women, including Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, and misled top company executives about his relationship with Alice Huang for more than a year before confirming the truth after days of denials.Nvidia gets new CEONvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO while the company’s board searches for a permanent successor. Huang had dozens of direct reports, but no clear succession plan. Huang still holds a more than 3.5% stake in Nvidia, making him one of its largest shareholders.Your child uses AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old saleswoman was found murdered inside the trial room of a clothing showroom in west Delhi's Moti Nagar on Saturday evening, with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old saleswoman was found murdered inside the trial room of a clothing showroom in west Delhi's Moti Nagar on Saturday evening, with police identifying a 29-year-old man as the prime suspect.The victim, identified as Shabnam, was allegedly attacked with a knife before the accused fled. Police have formed teams to trace and apprehend the suspect, identified as Suraj, a resident of Sudamapuri in Moti Nagar.Her body was discovered inside the trial room of Vastr Mahal, located at 6/18, Moti Nagar. She had a sharp injury on her neck, and a blood-stained knife was recovered near her body, police said.A woman claiming to have witnessed the events leading to the discovery of the body said Shabnam had previously worked for her before joining a shop directly opposite her workplace."The girl used to work for me... She had started working at a place right across from mine. At around 6.45 PM, I noticed her—I could see her shop from my own—sitting there and using her phone," the woman said.She said she received a call from Shabnam's employer around 7.30 pm, informing her that the young woman was missing after a man allegedly assaulted her."Around 7.30pm, I received a call from her employer, who said, 'I don't see Shabnam in the shop. A man came by and beat her up quite severely. Could you please go and check what happened? She is nowhere to be found, and she left the shop wide open.' I went over, but we couldn't find anything..." she said.The witness said two neighbours later arrived at the showroom, closed the shop and locked it around 8 pm. However, after checking the CCTV footage, they returned around 8.30 pm, suspecting that Shabnam might still be inside."Then, around 8.30pm, the men came back to me and said, 'Shabnam must still be inside—we checked the footage, and she never left. We only saw a man leave, but she didn't come out. Could you come inside with us to take a look?'" she said.The group entered the showroom while recording a video. The woman said they initially found nothing, before noticing Shabnam's scarf near the trial room."We went inside while recording a video, but we couldn't see anything at first. Then, my eyes fell toward the very back—the trial room—where I spotted her scarf (chunni) lying on the floor, and blood was seeping out from inside..."The woman said they immediately alerted the police and contacted Shabnam's parents."We immediately called the police and contacted Shabnam’s parents... Her throat had been slit, and she was lying on the floor, with blood everywhere," she said.A PCR call reporting a woman lying unconscious inside the showroom was received at Moti Nagar police station on November 14. A police team reached the spot and found Shabnam dead.Crime team personnel and forensic science laboratory experts subsequently inspected the scene and collected evidence. Her body was shifted to the mortuary of Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for a post-mortem examination.During the preliminary investigation, police found that two of the suspect's brothers are married to two sisters of the deceased.Based on a complaint lodged by Shabnam's brother, police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police teams later visited Suraj's residence but found it locked. articles.title: $20 million buried in forests, stashed in warehouses found in Hungary corruption probe
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, with some of the money allegedly buried in forests and hidden inside farm
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, with some of the money allegedly buried in forests and hidden inside farm buildings, warehouses and residential properties, as part of a bribery investigation involving former minister Miklos Sesztak, who served under ex-prime minister Viktor Orban.The recovery was announced by Hungary's National Asset Recovery and Protection Office late on Friday. The operation is part of a wider anti-corruption drive launched by Prime Minister Peter Magyar following his party's victory over Orban in the April election, ending the latter's 16-year rule."During searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location," the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said.Finance minister Andras Karman said a team of 12 State Treasury employees took eight hours to count the recovered money using banknote-counting machines.Magyar described the recovery as evidence of the end of what he called a "mafia" allegedly run by Orban's Fidesz party and its Christian Democrat allies during their years in power.The anti-corruption campaign, which Magyar has named "Operation Purgatory", is aimed at investigating allegations of graft linked to the previous administration. A survey by pollster Median, published by news website HVG this week, found that 70% of respondents considered the campaign "very important".Former minister denies links to recovered cashSesztak, who served as development minister under Orban from 2014 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to a request for comment on the asset recovery office's statement.However, Papp told local news website Telex that the seized cash did not belong to his client. He also said the bribery investigation involved other suspects.Sesztak is currently a member of parliament's Economic and Energy Affairs Committee.Orban's Fidesz party said it hoped the recovered money had no connection to the former minister."Since the change of regime, every lawmaker in Hungary has sworn an oath to abide by and enforce the law. Fidesz-KDNP (Christian Democrats) cannot associate itself with anyone who fails to do so. We trust that the images published by the NVVH (asset recovery office) have nothing to do with Miklos Sesztak," Fidesz wrote in a Facebook post.Bence Retvari, parliamentary group leader of the Christian Democrats, also called on Sesztak, the party's vice chair, to give up his parliamentary mandate while he seeks to clear his name."This is an individual criminal case, and the criminal proceedings must be kept strictly separate from our political community," Retvari said on Facebook."Peter Magyar wants to use it to portray the entire right as a criminal organisation. We reject this in the strongest possible terms!"Anti-corruption drive targets former Orban officialsThe investigation involving Sesztak is among several cases targeting former officials from Orban's government.In separate investigations, two former ministers and former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy have been arrested over corruption allegations. All have denied wrongdoing.Authorities have also detained Orban's brother in a people-smuggling case, which the former prime minister has dismissed as politically motivated revenge.Political scientist Gabor Torok said the images of the recovered cash were particularly damaging for Fidesz and could further weaken the party's public support.A Median survey showed that Fidesz's support had fallen to 16% of voters in November, down by half from its pre-election level.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ex-Met Police inspector lied about wife's death in Barbados hotel room, BBC learns
articles.summary: Warren Arter faced claims of sexually exploiting crime victims - his wife was found in a blood-stained room.
articles.body:
Warning: Contains graphic details of Rebekah Arter's death - and references to coercion and sexual abuse

A former Metropolitan Police detective, investigated for sexually exploiting vulnerable crime victims it was his job to protect, later lied about the death of his wife in a Barbados hotel room, BBC Panorama has learned.

Warren Arter first met his wife Rebekah after she reported domestic abuse to the Met. He then abused her for more than a decade. Her death two years ago has never been properly investigated.

Panorama can reveal failures by Barbados authorities to preserve evidence and interview hotel staff about Arter's suspicious behaviour before and after Rebekah's death, aged 47.

Despite a request from her family for assistance, the Met did not send detectives to the Caribbean island.

The Met told the BBC it took this decision because no allegation of criminality had been made.

Rebekah's family, speaking publicly for the first time, have told Panorama the Met failed her. The cause of her death is still not known with a coroner in the UK recording an open verdict.

We have also spoken to hotel staff who were called to the room in June 2024 after Arter rang reception to say his wife had collapsed.

Interviews with the staff, police sources - plus Arter's erratic communications following Rebekah's death - reveal:

Arter gave conflicting accounts - telling staff and Rebekah's family she had choked, fallen and banged her head, or he had woken up and found her dead

Evidence was not secured, vital forensic tests were not taken and Rebekah's organs were inexplicably "chopped up" by a pathologist in Barbados

Four days after Rebekah's death, a senior Met boss from its Gold Command was briefed about the incident in light of Arter's alleged offending - but it did not lead to officers travelling to the Caribbean island

Arter, 54, took his own life in HMP Wandsworth, days after he had returned from Barbados and been arrested for allegedly abusing another woman.

Rebekah had been escaping an abusive relationship when Arter investigated her case in 2006. The detective then pursued a relationship with her and moved in not long after.

Three years later, he was placed in charge of a unit in south-east London investigating rape cases.

Arter was later suspended by the Met and investigated over his conduct towards eight alleged victims by its watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) - but was never convicted.

Over the seven years he was suspended, Arter continued to receive his full detective inspector salary, before being dismissed in 2023 for drug offences.

All this time, he subjected Rebekah to sexual and domestic abuse, coercive control, and drugging, which the BBC has seen video evidence of.

Panorama has now spoken to several members of staff who were working at the luxury O2 Beach Club in Barbados on the night of Rebekah's death. All say Arter behaved suspiciously.

Two of them entered Arter's hotel room after he had called to say his wife was unwell. Both say it was immediately clear Rebekah was dead.

Andrew, a security guard, says he had to prevent Arter from going to a nearby street party, before emergency services arrived.

"So I'm asking him, why do you need to go when you have a bigger issue here?"

Andrew says Arter responded: "Oh, I just need to clear my head."

Watch Panorama: The Predator in the Police on BBC iPlayer from 0600 on Tuesday 17 November - or on BBC One at 21:00 that evening (not in Wales and Northern Ireland)

Arter then began crying "crocodile tears" and conducting performative CPR despite Rebekah's lips being blue, according to Andrew, who says Arter's explanation of what happened kept changing.

Initially, Arter told Andrew she had fallen near a chest of drawers - but her body was some distance away, near the kitchen. When police arrived, Andrew says he heard Arter tell them he had found her like that.

There was no sign of Rebekah having a head injury, Andrew says, despite bloodstains on the bed, the wall and the living room area.

Arter recorded a video of the room and sent it to family and friends in the UK.

"It looks like chocolate but it's blood," he can be heard saying.

Andrew says he told Arter to phone family in the UK - and then heard him tell them that she had been unwell.

"He was just trying to find the right story that fits and none of them added up," says Andrew.

The security guard says he told Barbadian police officers what he saw and gave a statement but was never formally interviewed.

Panorama has seen some of Arter's messages and spoken to Rebekah's friends and family who were contacted by him shortly after her death.

They reveal that Arter provided other possible causes of death - that Rebekah had "choked" or that her drink had been spiked.

These accounts are contradicted by Rebekah's daughter-in-law, Lacey, who says he told her they had both been asleep for 18 hours and he had woken up and found her dead.

"He was outright lying. He was forgetting what he was telling people," says Lacey.

Arter was briefly detained by Barbadian police but released a short time later.

One of the police officers who attended the room that night refused to share information with Panorama without payment. He still had a photograph of Rebekah's dead body on his phone.

Police in Barbados did not respond to our request for comment.

Other hotel staff members have told the BBC they were concerned about Arter's treatment of Rebekah during their stay.

Security supervisor Kenneth says Arter appeared "controlling" and "didn't allow Rebekah to do anything on her own". Rebekah also frequently appeared to be "intoxicated", he says.

A third member of staff, who worked on the front desk, says staff suspected Arter was "drugging" Rebekah.

Panorama has seen a video, filmed by Arter on his phone when she was still alive, which shows Rebekah clearly intoxicated. She is wearing the same clothes that she is pictured in after she died.

If you are in the UK and you have been affected by any of the issues in this story such as sexual abuse and violence , information and support is available at BBC Action Line

In the early hours of the morning after her death, during the staff member's night shift, Arter approached the hotel front desk to ask when Rebekah last had a massage in the hotel spa.

She says his question struck her as bizarre and felt like he was trying to get his story straight.

Meanwhile, back in the UK, Rebekah's son, Elliot, and his wife, Lacey, were becoming increasingly concerned after visiting the home she shared with Arter.

Inside, they say they found a variety of drugs and hidden CCTV cameras that Arter had rigged up in the house.

They also discovered photographs of Rebekah naked and bruised, involved in sexual acts, seemingly taken without her consent.

Four days after Rebekah's death, they went to Bexleyheath Police Station, the same station where Arter once led rape investigations, to report her death to the Met and raise concerns about his possible involvement.

"The front office staff said, 'Oh well it's happened in Barbados, it's a Barbados issue' - and tried to brush it off at first," says Elliot.

"The moment I gave Warren's name, it was like chaos - we had sergeants coming down to the front desk," says Lacey.

"But it really wasn't about Rebekah, it was more about Warren," she says.

That evening, an officer briefed a Gold Commander within the Met, a senior boss who decides how to respond to incidents. The Met did not send detectives to Barbados.

UK police forces can be asked to help investigate a death of a British national overseas - usually at the request of local police where the death occurred.

Under Foreign Office guidance, the case for such involvement is strengthened when families request assistance and there are credible concerns about the circumstances of the death, as there were in Rebekah's case.

The Met told the BBC it made immediate efforts to obtain information in order to assess whether to travel to Barbados but decided it would not be appropriate without an allegation of criminality.

An inquest in the UK later found that Rebekah's organs had been inexplicably "chopped up" into small pieces by a pathologist in Barbados.

This served no medical purpose and destroyed vital evidence, according to a UK pathologist who examined her body after it had been repatriated.

The inquest also established that key toxicology and histology tests - to look for signs of disease, injury or other changes in the body - were not conducted.

The coroner, Andrew Harris, said this raised the prospect of "deliberate concealment or obstruction of further investigation".

He also said that while bloodstains on bedclothes may be consistent with vomiting, he could not accept the cause of death determined by Barbadian authorities, aspiration pneumonitis - inflammation of the lungs - and delivered an open verdict.

He concluded that Rebekah's death likely involved intoxication and said unlawful killing could not be ruled out.

The inquest did not, however, consider Arter's alleged sexual exploitation of several other women whose cases he had investigated, to be within its scope.

Police in Barbados have previously said no marks of violence were found on Rebekah's body and there was nothing to suggest anything untoward - adding that they did not order toxicology tests because they believed she died from natural causes.

A week after Rebekah died, Arter flew back to the UK where he was arrested at Heathrow in connection with alleged sexual offences against another woman whose case he had investigated as a police officer in 2010. He was found dead in Wandsworth prison three days later.

In response to the BBC, Metropolitan Police Commander Simon Messinger said: "Our thoughts at this time remain with Rebekah Arter's family, who understandably have questions about the circumstances of her death.

"We would urge any victim survivors of rape and sexual offences - no matter how long ago a crime may have occurred - to reach out."

Elliot says his two young children will never know their grandmother.

"My daughter, my son - they're never gonna actually have any memories of her," he says.

"For the rest of my life, I'm never going to know how she's passed away."
