articles.title: An American family has five generations born on September 14; a baby boy born in 2025 helped them set a Guinness World Record spanning 118 years
articles.summary: Imagine being born into a family where your great-great-grandfather, great-grandmother, grandfather, mother and you all share the same birthday.
articles.body: Imagine being born into a family where your great-great-grandfather, great-grandmother, grandfather, mother and you all share the same birthday. Suddenly, arriving fashionably late is not an option. Neither is being born on September 15.For one American family, September 14 is not just another date on the calendar. It is practically a family heirloom. And with the arrival of a baby boy in 2025, the Bell and Harlow family has managed to turn a rather unusual birthday coincidence into a Guinness World Record. The pressure to perform must have been tremendous.Five generations, one birthday and a rather impressive family traditionThe story began in 1907, when Wilber Harlow was born on September 14. A postmaster who also owned the Harlow General Store in Brooks, Iowa, Wilber probably had no idea that his birthday would go on to become something of a family institution.42 years later, on September 14, 1949, Wilber and his wife welcomed their daughter, Addie Harlow. Two generations down, and the family was already sharing a surname and a birthday.The coincidence continued in 1972, when Addie gave birth to her son, Donald Harlow, on September 14. Donald, in turn, welcomed his daughter Emma in 1997, also on September 14.At this point, one might reasonably suspect that September 14 had been reserved exclusively for the Harlow family. But the universe was not quite finished with its little joke. In 2025, Emma and her husband Wyatt welcomed their son Arthur Bell. His due date? September 14. And, as if the family had not already made its point, Arthur arrived on the very same day as his mother, grandfather, great-grandmother and great-great-grandfather.That makes five generations born on the same calendar date, spanning 118 years. The achievement earned the American family the Guinness World Records title for the most generations born on the same day in recorded human history.A birthday party that requires a family treeMost families struggle to organise one birthday party without somebody forgetting to order the cake. The Bells and Harlows, meanwhile, have managed to combine five generations into one annual celebration. Imagine the sugar levels on that day.According to Guinness World Records, the family had been aware of its unusual streak for years. With four generations already sharing September 14, they knew they had something special. However, they held off on applying for the record because they had a rather ambitious idea: they wanted to see whether a fifth generation could join the club.When Emma discovered that her second child's due date could fall on the family birthday, the possibility suddenly became much more real. And when Arthur arrived on September 14, the family finally had its five-generation record."We kind of always knew that we held a record with four generations, we just never applied because we had that ambition to have the fifth on 14 September," Emma told Guinness World Records.Well, talk about setting the bar high for your children. Most parents are happy if their offspring remember to call on their birthday. The Harlows appear to have made the actual date of birth a family expectation.There is another curious detail to the story. The five birthdays also follow an alternating pattern of genders: boy, girl, boy, girl, boy. Wilber, Addie, Donald, Emma and Arthur have managed to keep the sequence going for more than a century.Sadly, Addie passed away in 2023 and never got to meet her great-grandson Arthur. However, she was part of the family's birthday celebrations for years. The gatherings usually involved heading to a restaurant and sharing a cake with candles, which must have required increasingly careful counting.When coincidence starts looking suspiciously like fateOf course, the internet had a few questions when the record came to light. And some were rather less sentimental than others.On Reddit, where the story attracted plenty of attention, users wondered whether the family had somehow managed to coordinate five births. Others joked about the pressure on successive generations to ensure that the next baby arrived on the correct date. One commenter even imagined the delivery room as a particularly tense countdown, with everyone waiting for the right moment.To be fair, it is an understandable question. Babies do not generally consult family calendars before deciding to make an entrance. Pregnancy due dates are estimates, and births can happen days or even weeks before or after them.Medical interventions can also make the timing of a delivery more predictable in some circumstances, but that does not mean the family necessarily planned every birth around September 14. Guinness records the coincidence, not a century-long exercise in scheduling pregnancies.Emma's grandfather, Donald, seemed to have a simpler explanation. "God works in beautiful ways," he said.And apparently, God has a rather strong preference for September birthdays.There is one more coincidence that makes the story even more unusual. Wilber and his wife Addie were married in Maryville, Missouri, the same place where Emma and Wyatt eventually met. It is a small detail, perhaps, but one that gives the family history an almost cinematic quality. The same date keeps coming around, and apparently, so does the same location.A record that takes a village (and several generations)Before the Bells and Harlows claimed the title, four generations sharing a birthday was already a recognised record. In fact, Guinness notes that the four-generation achievement had been held simultaneously by seven different families, with examples dating back to the 1800s. The fifth generation, however, gave the Harlows the distinction of becoming the sole record holders.This is not a record that can be achieved by one particularly talented individual, a gruelling training regime or an extraordinary display of endurance. It takes generations, a little luck and a coincidence that refuses to let go.Arthur is still very young, so he has plenty of time before he has to worry about breaking any records of his own. But he has already inherited a rather unusual family legacy. Somewhere down the line, he might even find himself explaining to his children why September 14 is a date that absolutely cannot be overlooked.Until then, the family has 118 years of birthdays to celebrate, one Guinness certificate to show for it, and a very good reason to order an exceptionally large cake every September. One can only hope the next generation is not already feeling the pressure.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
